name: Oils (omega-3, fish oil, coconut oil)
anchor: No sovereign government sets a heavy-metal maximum for a pet supplement in a human-food basis. The instruments that reach the exact cell are pet-feed and animal-feed instruments. Japan's Pet Food Safety Act is the strongest of them: the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food are statutory, pet-scoped and recorded on an as-sold basis, and they set lead at 3000, cadmium at 1000 and inorganic arsenic at 2000 ug/kg (jp_petfood_2021_pb_3000, jp_petfood_2021_cd_1000, jp_petfood_2021_ias_2000) and set nothing for the remaining panel analytes. The EU feed instruments follow (Directive 2002/32/EC complementary feed for pet animals, mineral feed and trace-element feed additives under Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003), then FDA CVM compliance policy, then China's pet-feed guidance, which is draft and gated out of the register in any event. NASC's quality guidelines are voluntary and non-binding and are not a sovereign source at all. Every one of these floors is one hundred to three hundred times looser than the corresponding value published here, and every one is named on the cell it reaches. HMTc treats the feed instruments as a disclosed floor and anchors every published cell on the strictest applicable AS-SOLD child-protective human-food sovereign maximum, following Category 17's human-grade over-compliance and Category 16's child-protective supplement rule together. Where no as-sold sovereign value exists in any jurisdiction (aluminium, total chromium, hexavalent chromium, methylmercury) the cell is a control: mandatory testing with a published method and escalation rule, and no invented ceiling.
native_basis_label: the supplement as sold (as-packaged concentrate) — dry weight for powders, chews, tablets and capsules, neat liquid for oils and drops; no reconstitution, dilution, or as-fed conversion is applied
scope_note: Neat oils and oil-based dosage forms sold as supplements for companion animals: marine oils (fish, krill, cod liver, algal), plant oils (coconut, flaxseed, hemp seed, olive) and emulsions or pump-dosed liquids built on them. The product is dosed as sold, so the native basis is the neat oil, not an as-fed diluted basis. Marine-derived material makes the methylmercury pathway credible for this row, so methylmercury is measured on every lot rather than only on reflex. Refining partitions most metals into the protein and phospholipid fractions, which lowers expected occurrence, but that is an occurrence expectation and does not relax any ceiling. Boundary rules from the HMTc taxonomy govern placement: the product must be intended for animal consumption as a supplement rather than as the sole or primary diet; anything bearing an AAFCO nutritional adequacy statement routes to Category 17 (Pet Foods); and a dental chew routes to Category 17 (pet chews), because its primary function is food or treat rather than supplementation.
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a register row the register itself classifies basis_class=as_sold. A pet supplement is dosed as sold: a scoop of powder, a chew, a capsule, a pump of neat oil. It is never reconstituted, and the 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion is confined to infant formula (CLAUDE.md Part 19), so no conversion is available to make a ready-to-feed liquid maximum comparable to an as-sold concentrate. The guard therefore blocks (a) every liquid/ready-to-feed limb of a form-split infant instrument, which the register classifies as_consumed, (b) the AU-NZ Schedule 19 'portion ordinarily consumed' rows, and (c) every animal-feed instrument, whose basis is a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification. Where a government instrument writes its own powder/liquid split and that instrument supplies the binding anchor, the guard mechanically selects the powder limb, which is what Method v2.0 step 4 requires: preserve the product-form split the government rule itself writes. That is the position on inorganic arsenic (EU 2023/915) and nickel (EU 2024/1987), the two cells where a form-split instrument still binds. It is not the position on lead, cadmium and total mercury: those three are anchored on Israel's FCS-2016 food-for-special-dietary-purpose limb, which is not form-split at all, so on those cells the guard does no limb selection and only confirms the row is written on the product as placed on market. Choosing the stricter liquid limb for an as-sold concentrate would be a silent basis conversion in the strict direction, which is still a conflation, and the as-consumed limbs declined on that ground are named cell by cell.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default), pet-supplement double over-compliance form: the exact cell's only sovereign maximum is an animal-feed instrument, which is disclosed as a floor and never used; every published value is a disclosed read-across to the strictest applicable as-sold child-protective human-food sovereign maximum in the product's native as-sold basis, or a control where no as-sold sovereign value exists. Never occurrence-derived.

Pb.basis: the supplement as sold (as-packaged concentrate) — dry weight for powders, chews, tablets and capsules, neat liquid for oils and drops; no reconstitution, dilution, or as-fed conversion is applied
Pb.label: Child-protective, human-grade read-across to the Israel Ministry of Health FCS-2016 lead maximum for food for special dietary purpose (row 16) — a binding sovereign maximum level written on the product as placed on market, and the strictest as-sold sovereign lead ceiling for a purpose-formulated finished food on the register. It is numerically equal to the lead action level the US FDA applies to processed food packaged for babies and young children, which is named as the co-equal confirming instrument. Adopted without any dilution or concentration allowance.
Pb.substantiation: No sovereign government sets a lead maximum for a pet supplement as such, so this cell is a disclosed read-across and not a direct maximum level. Why the Israeli 'food for special dietary purpose' limb is the adopted analog. Israel's FCS-2016 metal-contaminant table carries three limbs that could reach a purpose-formulated product: the infant and toddler formula limbs (rows 14, 14.1, 15, 15.1), the 'food for special dietary purpose' limb (Pb row 16, Cd row 15, tHg row 16), and a separate 'dietary supplements' limb (Pb row 17 at 3000, Cd row 16 at 1000, tHg row 15 at 100). HMTc declines the dietary-supplement limb for the reason Category 16 declines every adult-supplement floor: it is an adult-intake framework running one to three orders of magnitude above the child-food ceilings, and a companion animal receiving a concentrated daily dose is a small-bodied consumer. That leaves the formula limbs and the special-dietary-purpose limb, both of which sit inside this category's declared analog family — a finished, purpose-formulated food for a defined consumer, written on the product as placed on market — and Method v2.0 step 3 then requires the strictest applicable of them, which is the special-dietary-purpose limb in all three cells. The determination is stated rather than assumed: HMTc is not applying Israel's own classification of a supplement, which would be the 3000/1000/100 limb; it is applying Israel's strictest formulated-food ceiling to a product Israel does not regulate at all, and it says so. All three rows are binding national maximum levels, all three are written on the product as placed on market, and the register now classifies all three basis_class=as_sold in line with the rest of the instrument, so all three pass this row's basis guard on the same footing as the powder limbs they replace. The candidate set at the adopted value. Two instruments reach 10 ug/kg: the Israeli special-dietary-purpose row adopted here (il_fcs2016_pb_16_food_for_special_dietary_purpose_10), which is a binding national maximum level, and the US FDA final guidance action level for processed food packaged for babies and young children (fda2025_pb_baby_food_10), which is expressly nonbinding. Both are named. The Israeli row binds because a binding sovereign maximum level is the stronger instrument under Method v2.0 step 2; nothing turns on the choice numerically, because the two agree. Citation correction of record on this cell. An earlier version anchored lead on us_pb_processed-food-packaged-for-babies-and-y_10, which is a duplicate register row for the same January 2025 FDA guidance. Its status field read 'maximum level', which contradicted this cell's own prose describing the instrument as a final guidance action level, and its authority url pointed at a law-firm client alert rather than at the FDA guidance document. That row's status and url have been corrected in the register, and this cell no longer cites it. fda2025_pb_baby_food_10 is the canonical row for the 10 ug/kg limb, with fda2025_pb_root_baby_food_20 and fda2025_pb_dry_infant_cereal_20 for the two 20 ug/kg limbs. Full de-duplication of the pair, so that one register id survives per instrument limb, is a register-maintenance item recorded for the verified regulatory-fetch pathway and is not performed from inside a category config. The remaining as-sold child-food lead ceilings, all laxer and none adopted: the Israeli infant-formula powder limb (il_fcs2016_pb_15_1_infant_formula_powder_50), the EU baby-food and powdered-formula limbs (eu2023_pb_babyfood_cereal_20, eu2023_pb_formula_powder_20), the Codex cereal-based infant-food maximum (codex_pb_cereal-based-foods-for-infants-and-young_20) and the UK formula maximum (uk_pb_infant-formulae-and-follow-on-formulae-m_50). Register-tagging note, recorded because the earlier version of this cell depended on the gap. Most Israel FCS-2016 rows carried the register's canonical as-sold wording in their free-text basis field ('product as placed on market') with an empty basis_class cell, so a basis guard written against basis_class could not see them; the special-dietary-purpose rows were in that state and were therefore invisible to both the guard and this row's audit scope. That was an internal tagging gap, not a legal or basis distinction, and it has been closed: every FCS-2016 row whose basis reads 'product as placed on market' now carries basis_class=as_sold, matching the instrument's own already-tagged powder rows, and 'special dietary' has been added to every subcategory's audit_scope so the limb is scanned rather than merely named. This value is identical to the lead ceiling the live HMTc Category 16 human-supplement standard publishes, so the pet standard is not laxer than the human standard on lead. with China's draft pet-feed guidance in the same range. Japan's Pet Food Safety Act is disclosed on the same footing and is the one pet-scoped floor that is neither draft nor guidance: the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food set statutory maxima that the register records on an as-sold basis for lead, cadmium and inorganic arsenic only (jp_petfood_2021_pb_3000, jp_petfood_2021_cd_1000, jp_petfood_2021_ias_2000), and set nothing for the remaining panel analytes. Category 17, the live pet-foods standard this category builds on, names the same three rows, and Category 18 names them here for the same reason. They run one hundred to three hundred times above the corresponding values published in this category. They are outside this compiler's audit scan because Japan sits outside this category's credible-regulator set, not because any basis mechanism blocks them; the honest statement is that HMTc declines them as a floor, not that the machinery could not see them. The human food-supplement floor (eu2023_cd_food_supplements_1000, th_moph414_2020_pb_food_supplement_1000, il_fcs2016_pb_17_dietary_supplements_3000, il_fcs2016_cd_16_dietary_supplements_except_listed_categories_1000, il_fcs2016_thg_15_dietary_supplements_100, gso193_2021_thg_food_supplements_100, asean2017_pb_health_supplements_10000, hsa2024_pb_health_supplements_10000) is likewise disclosed and never used. Of the three floors, only the EU feed rows are unreachable by construction: they carry a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification, so this row's basis guard blocks them and the audit scan drops any row whose basis names feed. The human food-supplement rows are not blocked by any mechanism at all — Israel's supplement rows are classified as-sold and match this row's audit scope — so they are declined by the declared analog-family filter alone, which is exactly why that filter is stated openly in _category.method_note instead of being left to the machinery to enforce silently.

tAs.source_scope: Infant Milk substitute and Infant foods
tAs.label: Child-protective, human-grade read-across to the FSSAI total-arsenic maximum for infant milk substitute and infant foods, which the register records on an as-sold basis (the source column is parts per million by weight with no reconstitution basis stated). Total arsenic is a total-element cell in its own right and additionally gates the inorganic-arsenic speciation reflex; the toxic species is limited separately.
tAs.substantiation: No regulator in the default credible set sets a total-arsenic maximum for any child food: the EU, UK, Codex, US, Canadian and FSANZ instruments regulate inorganic arsenic only. The as-sold sovereign child-food total-arsenic rows are FSSAI (the strictest, adopted here), the Singapore Food Agency baby-food and infant-formula rows (sg_foodregs_2026_baby_food_tas_100, sg_foodregs_2026_infant_formula_tas_100), a Chinese milk-powder row and the Israeli formula-powder row (il_fcs2016_tas_14_1_infant_and_toddler_formulas_powder_1000). FSSAI is admitted to this category's credible-regulator set for that reason and it makes the standard stricter, not more convenient. The animal-feed floor that legally governs this cell is disclosed and never used: in the EU a pet supplement is complementary feed for pet animals or a feed additive under Directive 2002/32/EC and Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003 (register rows eu2002_32_pb_complementary_feed_10000, eu2002_32_cd_pet_complementary_feed_2000, eu2002_32_tas_complementary_feed_4000, eu2002_32_thg_mineral_feed_200, eu2002_32_pb_mineral_feed_15000, eu2002_32_cd_mineral_feed_materials_2000, eu2002_32_tas_mineral_feed_12000 and the trace-element and binder/anti-caking additive rows), with China's draft pet-feed guidance in the same range. The FSSAI row's free-text basis previously read 'as consumed' while its basis_class read as_sold and its own notes recorded the as-sold correction against the FSSAI 2011 primary text, whose column header is parts per million by weight with no reconstitution basis stated — a half-applied correction that left the human-readable field contradicting the machine-readable one. iAs.source_scope: infant formulae, follow-on formulae, food for special medical purposes intended for infants and young children, and young-child formulae placed on the market as powder

The liquid limb (eu2023_ias_formula_liquid_10) governs a ready-to-feed liquid, is classified as_consumed, and is not applicable to an as-sold concentrate. The rice-specific child-food rows (fda2020_ias_infant_rice_cereal_100, us_ias_rice-cereals-for-infants-all-types-white_100, ca_ias_rice-based-foods-intended-specifically-f_100, uk_ias_rice-destined-for-the-production-of-food_100) are laxer and commodity-scoped. Rice-derived carriers (rice maltodextrin, rice flour, rice hull) are a recognised inorganic-arsenic route into supplement dosage forms and are held to this ceiling, not to the rice-commodity ceiling. Stricter-unselected audit disposition for this cell. The audit scan, whose scope is now identical on all seven subcategories, surfaces exactly one stricter row on every one of them: the Israeli fluid-milk inorganic-arsenic ceiling il_fcs2016_ias_1_milk_10. The general rule, stated once in _category.method_note and applied identically wherever it arises: the register's basis_class records whether a limit is written on the product as sold or as consumed, but it does not record how much water the commodity contains. Divergence from HMTc Category 16, disclosed. Category 16 anchors inorganic arsenic on eu2023_ias_formula_liquid_10 and publishes 10 ug/kg for as-sold solid supplements; Category 18 declines that row because the register classifies it as_consumed, and reads the powder limb of the same instrument at 20 ug/kg instead. This category publishes the laxer of the two numbers and says so. The reason is the basis rule rather than a policy preference, and no stricter as-sold sovereign inorganic-arsenic instrument exists anywhere in the credible set for a non-water, non-fluid-commodity matrix, so there is nothing available to close the gap without performing the conversion Method v2.0 forbids. The reconciliation belongs on the Category 16 side and is logged with the aluminium item. Row-specific applicability determination for the oils subcategory, which the generic as-sold sentence does not reach. This row's native basis is a neat liquid and its anchor is the powder limb of an instrument whose split axis is product form, so the choice has to be justified on this row rather than inherited from the powder rows. The EU and Israeli splits do not divide powder from liquid as physical states; they divide product as placed on market from product as reconstituted for feeding. The liquid limb governs formula that has already been made up with water, which is why the register classifies it as_consumed, and its lower number is the same substance measured after roughly a sevenfold to eightfold dilution. Al.rationale: No government anywhere sets an aluminium contaminant maximum for a food on an as-sold basis. The only sovereign food aluminium numbers on the register are the FSANZ Schedule 19 infant-formula rows — aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500 at 500 ug/kg for non-soy infant, follow-on and special-medical-purpose formula, and aunz_sch19_al_formula_soy_1000 at 1000 ug/kg for soy-based formula — which are written on a 'portion ordinarily consumed' reconstituted basis the register classifies as_consumed and which no permitted conversion makes comparable to an as-sold concentrate, and the Chinese GB 2760 baked-goods and starch-noodle rows, which are permitted food-additive residue allowances for alum firming and leavening agents rather than contaminant ceilings. The remaining aluminium rows are drinking-water guideline values and a plastics food-contact specific migration limit, both different matrices in different bases. Adopting the reconstituted FSANZ value for an as-sold powder would be a silent eight-fold basis conversion in the strict direction; adopting an additive-residue allowance as a contaminant ceiling would misdescribe the instrument. Neither is supportable, so no number is invented and testing is mandatory instead. This is the same disposition HMTc Category 17 publishes for aluminium in pet foods. Divergence from HMTc Category 16, disclosed here because this is the one cell where Category 18 publishes no ceiling and the live human-supplement standard publishes one. Category 16 reads aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500 across to as-sold solid supplements and publishes 500 ug/kg, describing it there as the only government aluminium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction. Category 18 declines the same row on basis grounds, and the consequence is stated plainly rather than left to be discovered: a pet supplement certified under Category 18 receives no numeric aluminium ceiling, only mandatory measurement and a trend control, where a human supplement certified under Category 16 receives 500 ug/kg. Category 18's basis reasoning is the more rigorous of the two, and the reconciliation belongs on the Category 16 side, which is the side performing an undisclosed as-consumed to as-sold read; it is logged for that purpose and is not resolved from inside this config.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium on every lot by ICP-MS after closed-vessel microwave acid digestion. Results are trended per SKU and per raw-material lot; a step change against the SKU's own established baseline, or any result attributable to a declared aluminium-bearing processing aid, anti-caking agent, colour lake or clay/zeolite carrier, triggers a formulation and raw-material investigation before release. Aluminium results are reported on the certificate rather than suppressed.

Cr.rationale: No government sets a total-chromium maximum for any child food or any supplement. The complete set of as-sold total-chromium rows inside this category's credible-regulator set is: the Hong Kong Cap. 132V per-commodity rows for vegetables, pulses, cereals, meat, poultry, fish and shellfish (hk_cap132v_crtotal_vegetables-other-than-pulses_500 at 500 ug/kg and its siblings at 1000 ug/kg); the two Indian FSSAI specifications, in_fssai2015_crtotal_gelatin_10000 for gelatin at 10,000 ug/kg and in_fssai2016_crtotal_001_all_fishery_products_12000 for all fishery products at 12,000 ug/kg; and the US colour-additive purity specifications at 21 CFR 73 and 74 (us_fda_21cfr74_74_101_cr-total_50000, us_fda_21cfr74_74_203_cr-total_50000 and their siblings), which are ingredient specifications for certified colours rather than food ceilings. None is adopted. Switzerland's gelatine and collagen specifications (ch_vhk_2026_cr-total_gelatine_10000, ch_vhk_2026_cr-total_kollagen_10000) are named as an outside-the-credible-set comparator only: Switzerland is not in this category's credible-regulator set, so those rows could not anchor this cell whatever the disposition, and an earlier version of this rationale wrongly described one of them as a member of the set. The Hong Kong rows are raw whole-commodity ceilings, mostly written on wet commodities, and reading one across to a concentrated extract or dried botanical would silently change the concentration basis. The gelatin, collagen and fishery-product rows are ingredient and commodity specifications rather than finished-product contaminant ceilings — the gelatin and collagen figures reflect chrome-tanned hide processing and the fishery-product figure is a whole-commodity value — and together with the colour-additive specifications they sit so far above any plausible finished-product result that adopting one would replace a real control with a ceiling no product would ever breach. Declining them is therefore the stricter disposition, not the laxer one: what is published instead is mandatory total-chromium measurement on every lot, a reflex to hexavalent-chromium speciation, and a zero-tolerance failure rule on the species that actually carries the hazard. Trivalent chromium is nutritionally essential and the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, controlled separately. No number is invented; total chromium is measured on every lot and gates the hexavalent-chromium reflex.
Cr.reference_method: Total chromium on every lot by ICP-MS after closed-vessel microwave acid digestion. Any total-chromium result at or above the reflex trigger set in the category's testing schedule, and any total-chromium result that is elevated against the SKU's own baseline, requires hexavalent-chromium speciation before release.

Cr-VI.rationale: No government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for any food, any supplement or any pet product. Every hexavalent-chromium row on the register is a migration limit for toys, a drinking-water maximum contaminant level, or a content limit for textiles, leather, fertiliser and electrical equipment, all of which are different matrices in different bases and none of which is a dietary ceiling. A not-material determination is deliberately not claimed: the method-artifact argument that hexavalent chromium reduces to trivalent chromium holds in an acidic reducing food matrix, but this category routinely contains dry alkaline mineral and geologic carriers (bentonite, kaolin, zeolite, diatomaceous earth, calcium and magnesium salts) in which hexavalent chromium is not reliably reduced, so the claim would not be substantiable across the row. Control is the fail-safe and is what is published: hexavalent chromium is bounded by total chromium, which is measured on every lot, and any quantifiable hexavalent chromium fails certification.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total chromium on every lot by ICP-MS. Hexavalent chromium by EPA 3060A alkaline digestion with IC-ICP-MS, EPA 6800 or EN 15192, run on any lot that trips the total-chromium reflex trigger and on any lot whose formulation declares a mineral, clay, zeolite or geologic carrier. Quantifiable hexavalent chromium at the method limit of quantification is a certification failure, not a deviation.
